item.title: Houthis seize key Yemeni Red Sea port, sources say, threatening global energy flows
item.description:
Iran and its proxies move closer to full control of two shipping chokepoints as regional conflict widens Yemen’s Houthi rebels are making a concerted drive to take full control of the country’s Red Sea coast, claiming control of the key port of Mocha, in the most serious wave of fighting with the Saudi-backed government in years. Seizure of the coast would be a strategic disaster for Saudi Arabia and the US, taking Iran and its proxies closer to full control of two chokepoints for western shipping on opposite sides of the Arabian peninsula: the Bab al-Mandeb at the southern end of the Red Sea and the strait of Hormuz in the Gulf. item.title: Apple's new foldable iPhone: expensive gadget or bold statement?
item.description:
John Ternus, Apple's new CEO, unveiled the tech giant's latest smartphone on Wednesday. The foldable iPhone Duo will go on sale on October 23rd starting at $1,999, making it the most expensive iPhone to date. The move is a bid to comfort the US company's position at the top of the global smartphone market. item.title: A pilot of the Amazon cargo plane in Miami crash warned it was coming in too fast
item.description:
One of the pilots of the Amazon cargo plane that crashed in Miami last weekend, killing five people on the ground, repeatedly warned the other pilot the aircraft was "too fast" during the final approach and after touchdown, according to newly released information from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB). The pilots have been identified as Capt. Joseph Carroll, 55, and First Officer Jaime Felipe Silva Molina, 37, both of cargo airline 21 Air. The NTSB did not identify which pilot was making the warnings or which pilot was receiving them as they approached Miami International Airport on Sunday. The warnings continued for nearly two minutes, but the receiving pilot never gave "a consistent verbal response" to them, according to the NTSB's summary of the cockpit voice recorder. item.title: French Football Federation withdraws support for FIFA President Infantino
item.description:
France will not support the candidacy of Gianni Infantino, who is running for a new term as FIFA president in March 2027, the French Football Federation announced on Thursday. The FFF is aligning itself with the position of other European federations such as Belgium, Italy, Scotland, Sweden and Wales, who have also publicly withdrawn support for Infantino. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin reports.

item.title: Newsom suspended the death penalty. Will he go even further?
item.description:
A gurney is removed from the death penalty chamber at San Quentin State Prison on March 13, 2019. Photo by the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation via AP You could be forgiven for thinking capital punishment is all but dead in California. In 2019, Gov. Gavin Newsom halted executions and removed the gas chamber chair from San Quentin. Yet 546 men and 18 women are still sentenced to death in the state. A new analysis from The Marshall Project and CalMatters finds this accounts for one-quarter of all death sentences in the U.S. That leaves Newsom facing a monumental decision . As he prepares to leave office, he’s under pressure from local advocates and international human rights organizations to commute all 562 sentences, instead handing the inmates life without parole.
